DGEN-CTX-G2.title: Hollis & Reyes kitchen remodel quote HR-2291
DGEN-CTX-G2.text:
HOLLIS & REYES RENOVATION - KITCHEN REMODEL QUOTE
Quote number: HR-2291
Client: Dana and Chris Whitfield, 14 Birchwood Lane
Prepared by: Luis Reyes, project manager
Quote valid for 30 days from the date of issue.

SCOPE SUMMARY
Full remodel of the existing kitchen (approx. 180 sq ft), including a new island with seating, new cabinets, quartz countertops, updated plumbing and electrical, new flooring, backsplash, and paint. Layout stays the same except for the island.

LINE ITEMS
1. Demolition and disposal of existing cabinets, counters and flooring: $3,200
2. Cabinets - semi-custom shaker style, 22 linear feet, painted finish: $14,800
3. Countertops - quartz, 3 cm, eased edge, one undermount sink cutout: $6,900
4. Island - 6 ft island with seating overhang for 3 stools, including its cabinets and quartz top: $5,600
5. Plumbing - relocate dishwasher supply, new sink and faucet install (fixtures by client): $3,400
6. Electrical - 6 recessed lights, under-cabinet lighting, 4 new outlets, island outlet: $4,100
7. Flooring - luxury vinyl plank, 180 sq ft, including underlayment: $3,300
8. Backsplash - tile material allowance of $900 plus installation labor of $750: $1,650
9. Paint - walls and ceiling, two coats: $1,200
10. Permits and inspections: $850

Subtotal: $45,000

CONTINGENCY
We recommend a contingency reserve of 10% of the subtotal ($4,500). The contingency is NOT part of the contract price. It is only billed if hidden conditions are found (for example rot, outdated wiring, or subfloor damage), and only after written approval from the client.

WHAT THE CABINET LINE INCLUDES
Cabinet boxes, doors and drawer fronts, soft-close hinges and drawer slides, crown molding to the ceiling, filler panels, and installation.

WHAT THE CABINET LINE DOES NOT INCLUDE
Cabinet hardware (knobs and pulls), interior organizers such as pull-out trash or spice racks, and glass-front doors. These can be added by change order.

GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
Appliances and appliance installation, hauling away old appliances, drywall repair beyond 40 sq ft, and any work outside the kitchen footprint.

OPTION: REMOVE THE ISLAND
If the client chooses to remove the island, line 4 ($5,600) is deducted in full. Because the new flooring would then need to be patched and leveled where the island footprint was planned, an island-removal flooring adjustment of $600 is added. No other line items change.

SCHEDULE
Estimated duration: 6 to 7 weeks from demolition to final walkthrough. Our earliest available start date is June 9, provided the signed contract and deposit are received by May 16. After May 16 the next available start is in late August.

PAYMENT TERMS
Deposit: $3,000 due at signing to reserve the start date.
Second payment: 40% of the contract price when cabinets are delivered.
Third payment: 30% of the contract price when countertops are installed.
Final payment: the remaining balance after the final walkthrough and punch list are complete.
All payments by check or bank transfer. Card payments carry a 3% processing fee.

CHANGE ORDERS
Any change to scope, materials, or layout after signing requires a written change order with the price agreed before the work is done. Verbal agreements with crew members are not binding.

WARRANTY
Workmanship is warrantied for 2 years from the final walkthrough. Manufacturer warranties apply to cabinets, countertops and flooring.

CLIENT RESPONSIBILITIES
Choose tile, faucet and sink by the date given in the selections schedule. Clear the kitchen and adjacent pantry before demolition day. Provide access to a bathroom for the crew.

Questions: Luis Reyes, Hollis & Reyes Renovation.

PI-A:JD.title: the job description the user is targeting
PI-A:JD.text:
SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER, PAYMENTS & LEDGER
Tallowmarket, Inc. | Denver, CO

ABOUT TALLOWMARKET
Tallowmarket is a B2B marketplace where independent restaurants buy directly from regional farms and ranches. Our Payments & Ledger group moves about $1.1B a year through escrowed payouts to more than 6,500 growers. We are a team of 140 people, about 55 of them in engineering. Our backend is Go on PostgreSQL, with Kafka between services and Temporal for long-running payment workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own services in the money path: escrow holds, split payouts to growers, refunds and chargebacks.
- Design and evolve Harrow, our double-entry ledger built on PostgreSQL, as volume grows from 400,000 to a projected 1.5 million ledger entries per day.
- Improve the reliability of the nightly settlement batch that runs at 02:00 Mountain Time and must finish before banks open.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor mid-level engineers on the team.
- Join the on-call rotation, currently one week in six.
- Partner with Finance and Risk on reconciliation and audit requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING
- 5+ years of professional backend experience in Go, Java or Kotlin.
- Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: indexing, locking, isolation levels, and safe online migrations.
- Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, Kinesis or similar) and idempotent processing.
- A track record of leading multi-engineer projects from design doc to launch.
- Clear written communication; we make most decisions in design docs.

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work on a double-entry ledger or a payments platform.
- Experience reducing PCI DSS scope.
- Stripe Connect or Adyen for Platforms integration experience.
- Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid: in our Denver LoDo office Tuesday through Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible. Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to the Denver metro area.

COMPENSATION
Base salary band: $172,000 - $208,000 USD, plus equity and a 6% 401(k) match. This role is leveled at L5 (Senior).

INTERVIEW PROCESS
Recruiter screen (30 minutes), a 60-minute ledger design exercise, a Go coding session, and a values conversation with our Director of Engineering, Imani Castellanos.

Tallowmarket is an equal opportunity employer.

DGEN-CTX-I1.text:
Harbor Point Rowing Club - Spring Boat Maintenance Log

Week of April 7
The eight "Gull" had a loose rigger on seat 5. Bolts replaced and torqued. The four "Tern" came back with a cracked fin after hitting debris near the north buoy; it is out of service until the replacement fin arrives, expected in two weeks.

Week of April 14
All oars inspected. Three sculling blades had chipped tips and were sent for repair. Please rinse oars with fresh water after every row; salt build-up is loosening the collars.

Week of April 21
Launch motor serviced (spark plug, fuel filter). The launch now has a new kill cord, and coaches must wear it at all times. The dock ramp's left side is slippery at low tide, so carry boats on the right side until the anti-slip strips are replaced.

Reminders
Log every row on the sheet by the boathouse door: boat name, crew, time out, time in. Report any damage the same day, even small scratches. Singles may not go out when the wind flag is red. Lifejackets for launch passengers are in the blue locker.

Next maintenance day: volunteers needed to re-varnish the wooden oars. Sign up with Glen.

DGEN-CTX-G1.title: Okafor family Lisbon and Porto itinerary
DGEN-CTX-G1.text:
Okafor Family Trip - Lisbon and Porto (6 days)
Prepared by: Adaeze Okafor. Travellers: Adaeze, Tomi, and the kids Kemi (11) and Dayo (8).

FLIGHTS
Outbound: Atlantica Air flight AT 418, departs Newark 9:40 PM on day 0, lands Lisbon (LIS) at 11:15 AM on day 1. Checked bags: 2 included on the booking.
Return: Atlantica Air flight AT 419, departs Porto (OPO) 12:30 PM on day 6. Plan to be at OPO by 10:30 AM.

LISBON HOTEL (days 1 to 4)
Casa Rio Hotel, Rua dos Remedios 41, Alfama. Family room, confirmation CR-77310.
Check-in from 3:00 PM. Early bag drop is free from 10:00 AM. Check-out by 11:00 AM.
Airport to hotel: pre-booked van with Lusotransfer, about 35 minutes. The driver waits up to 60 minutes after landing, then the booking is cancelled with no refund (EUR 48).

DAY 1 - Arrive, Alfama
Land, van to hotel, drop bags, lunch near the hotel.
Alfama walking tour with Marta (Sete Colinas Walks), meeting at Largo das Portas do Sol at 4:30 PM. Duration 2.5 hours, mostly stairs, not stroller friendly. Tickets EUR 38 per adult, EUR 19 per child, already paid and non-refundable. The guide will move us to the 6:00 PM group once if we message her by 2:00 PM the same day.
Dinner: no reservation, keep it easy.

DAY 2 - Belem
Tram 15 to Belem around 9:30 AM. Jeronimos Monastery timed entry 10:30 AM (tickets on Adaeze's phone). Pasteis at the bakery after. Afternoon at the MAAT riverside park for the kids. Back by 5:00 PM.

DAY 3 - Sintra day trip
Train from Rossio station, trains roughly every 20 minutes, about 40 minutes each way. Pena Palace timed entry 11:00 AM. Pack lunch. Last comfortable train back around 6:00 PM. This is the long walking day, so the kids need proper shoes.

DAY 4 - Lisbon to Porto
Leave Casa Rio at 9:15 AM by taxi (about 20 minutes, book at the front desk the night before).
Train: Alfa Pendular 10:09 AM from Lisboa Santa Apolonia, arrives Porto Campanha 1:02 PM. Four tickets, car 3, seats 41 to 44. Tickets can be changed up to 15 minutes before departure for a EUR 5 fee per ticket. After departure, missed tickets are not refundable.
From Campanha, metro line to Trindade, then 8-minute walk to the apartment.
Porto apartment (Ribeira Flats, host: Nuno): check-in from 3:00 PM. Nuno wants our arrival time by 12:00 noon on day 4. Late check-in after 8:00 PM costs EUR 20.
Evening: Livraria Lello timed entry 5:30 PM (4 tickets, EUR 10 each, redeemable against a book). Entry slots cannot be moved on the day.

DAY 5 - Porto
Morning boat ride on the Douro (six bridges cruise), 10:00 AM from Cais da Ribeira, 50 minutes. Afternoon free. Dinner booked at Tasca do Largo at 7:30 PM, table for 4.

DAY 6 - Home
Check out of the apartment by 10:00 AM, taxi to OPO (about 25 minutes). Flight AT 419 at 12:30 PM.

BUDGET NOTES
Total trip budget excluding flights: EUR 3,200. Hotels and apartment are already paid. Daily food budget EUR 120 for the four of us. Keep EUR 200 cash for taxis and small cafes.

EMERGENCY CONTACTS
Casa Rio front desk: +351 21 000 4471. Nuno (Porto host): +351 91 000 2288. Travel insurance: Harborline Travel, policy HT-5520931.

items.question: Explain why the sky is blue at noon but orange at sunset, in a way my seven year old will get.
items.answer: Sunlight looks white, but it's really all the colors mixed together. Air is full of tiny bits that bounce the blue light around the whole sky, so at noon you see blue everywhere. At sunset, the light travels a long, low path, and the blue gets scattered away before it reaches you, leaving the reds and oranges.
